Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — ReqClarifyBench benchmark (341 tasks, LLM user simulator with 3 personas, 3 new metrics); compares 6 LLMs, base model vs coding-agent harness (Claude Code, Codex), and intent vs direct vs clarified requirement document as input to code generation

Interactive requirement clarification before implementation ('requirement-driven development paradigm'): LLM asks questions from a vague intent, writes a requirement document, which is then implemented. Compared inputs to code generation: initial intent / directly generated requirement document / interactively clarified requirement document. Harnesses: Claude Code and Codex (versions Not stated)

Requirement document (structured, atomic requirements; ground truth with requirement-artifact traceability, validated against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 criteria); clarification Q&A history. Generated documents format: Not stated beyond 'requirement document'

Vague intent -> multi-turn clarification (LLM decides what to ask and when to stop, max 20 rounds) -> requirement document -> code generation (RQ5, Codex + GPT-5.6-Sol). Authors suggest decoupling: base model for requirements, coding-agent harness for implementation
The (simulated) user answers clarification questions; no human review of documents or code during runs. Humans (two authors) validated the benchmark ground truth and the persona simulator
Requirements/specification phase (clarification + requirement document) for all; full flow to code only in RQ5 (one configuration)

Not classifiable (closest to spec-first: requirement document written before coding and not maintained); authors' wording: 'requirement-driven development paradigm', requirement document as 'intermediate representation between user intent and code implementation'
New projects (repository-level generation from scratch: games, mini-apps, websites)
341 tasks (MiniAppBench 100, GameCraft-Bench 140, WebGen-Bench 101); ground-truth docs avg 193 atomic requirements, 2,380 tokens; intents avg 13 tokens
Game development, mini-apps (interactive HTML), web development

Simulated users (GPT-5.6-Sol, temperature 0.7) with three personas from SWE-chat: Expert Nitpicker, Vague Requester, Mind Changer; persona fidelity checked by 2 annotators on 180 cases (accuracy 95.8%, kappa 0.892)
None measured (tokens/time motivate the study but are not reported); number of clarification rounds (stopping behavior) reported

None

Clarification effectiveness: Effective Question Rate (EQR, share of questions clarifying >= 1 atomic requirement), AvgClarified (atomic requirements per question); stopping round; round-wise clarification dynamics

Automatic: interaction logs; BERTScore; LLM-as-judge (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, temperature 0; 91.5% accuracy on 200 manually annotated cases) for ReqAlign and clarified requirements; source benchmarks' automated protocols for code. Benchmark ground truth reconstructed by LLM and validated by two authors

Tasks: ReqClarifyBench (341). Configurations: 6 LLMs x 3 personas (clarification); with vs without clarification (RQ3); base model vs coding-agent harness for 2 models (RQ4); 3 inputs to Codex + GPT-5.6-Sol for code (RQ5, scores averaged over personas). Baselines: direct document without clarification; initial intent for code. Held constant: user simulator (GPT-5.6-Sol, temp 0.7), task inputs, persona settings, interaction protocol, prompt templates, judge, max 20 rounds; evaluated LLMs temp 0. Acceptance tests: source benchmarks' behavioral protocols for code. Repetitions: Not stated (single run implied). Human intervention: none

GPT-5.6-Sol best document quality (ReqAlign 0.727, +26.0% over Claude Opus 5) but lowest clarification effectiveness; Gemini-3.1-Pro best EQR (0.334) but ReqAlign 0.357. Personas: mean ReqAlign 0.609 (EN) vs 0.433 (VR), 0.439 (MC). Clarification improves BERTScore 0.664 -> 0.712 (+7.2%) and ReqAlign 0.212 -> 0.494 (+133.1%; 83.8% GLM to 241.3% Qwen). Harnesses raise EQR/AvgClarified but lower document quality (ReqAlign EN -15.2% Claude, -24.0% GPT). Code: intent < direct doc < clarified doc on all 3 benchmarks (e.g., MiniApp 0.451 -> 0.543 -> 0.943). Significance: not tested

Distinguished models, personas and settings on document quality and clarification metrics. Repeatable: code, data and prompts released (Zenodo); single runs at temperature 0, no variance reported. Validation: persona simulator (95.8%, kappa 0.892), judge (91.5% on 200 cases). Limitations stated: simulated users may not capture real diversity; possible protocol/prompt errors; ground-truth document quality

Threats: reliability of LLM user simulation (external); errors in protocol, prompts, configuration (internal); quality of reconstructed ground-truth documents (construct). Implications: LLMs should proactively clarify before implementation; writing a requirement document helps even without feedback; decouple requirements (base model) from implementation (coding-agent harness)
